title: Every sensor reports 0, but Temp::read() returns 21. Tap the bug.
explain: sample() takes Sensor by value. Passing a Temp copies only the Sensor part. This is object slicing. The copy is a plain Sensor, so read() returns 0. Pass by reference or pointer: const Sensor& (if read() is const) or Sensor&.

title: The sensor sends temperature big-endian. 25.00 C shows as a huge wrong value. Tap the bug.
explain: The first byte on the wire is the most significant. from_le_bytes treats the first byte as the least significant, so 0x09C4 becomes 0xC409. Use from_be_bytes when the datasheet says big-endian. Always check byte order in the datasheet.

title: ARM GCC (plain char is unsigned). After the UART is idle, this loop never ends. Tap the bug.
explain: On ARM plain char is unsigned. -1 is stored as 255, and 255 is never equal to -1. The loop never stops. It also cannot tell the byte 0xFF from 'empty'. Keep the result in an int and compare that int.

pr.title: Use std::clamp for PWM duty
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: Replace the hand-written if chain with std::clamp. Same limits, less code.

explain: Correct. All three arguments are int, so there is no type mix. std::clamp(v, lo, hi) needs lo <= hi, and 0 <= 255 is true. It returns a reference, but the function returns int by value, so nothing dangles. Approve.

pr.title: Pack event flags into bitfields
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: Saves RAM: two flags now share one byte. The ISR sets rx, main clears tx.

explain: Both bitfields live in one byte. Writing one of them is a read-modify-write of that whole byte. If the ISR fires between the read and the write in main, its rx = 1 is lost. With separate bytes, each write is one store. Saving one byte of RAM is not worth a lost event. Keep separate flags, or use atomics.

pr.title: Use a short delay in the blink task
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: Timer needs extra setup. cortex_m::asm::delay is simpler and works the same.

explain: asm::delay is a busy loop. It never gives control back to the executor, so every other task on this executor stops for the whole delay. Timer::after_millis(500).await suspends only this task. In async code, never block. Always await.

title: Send the same frame twice. What happens?
explain: send takes the Vec by value, so the first call moves it. In the second loop turn frame is already gone: error 'use of moved value'. Pass &frame (and take &[u8]) or call frame.clone(). The compiler stops a double use before it runs.

title: What does this print?
explain: The two branches of ?: get a common type. int and unsigned int become unsigned int. So x (-1) turns into 4294967295, even though the condition picks x. Then 4294967295 > 0 is true: 1. Mixing signed and unsigned values hides sign bugs.

title: A 0.1 Ω shunt measures a 2 A motor current. How much heat does the shunt make, and which resistor rating is safe?
explain: P = I² x R = 2 x 2 x 0.1 = 0.4 W. A 0.25 W resistor would be overloaded. Use a rating at least 2x higher: 1 W. Also the shunt drops 0.2 V (V = I x R), which the ADC amplifier must handle.

title: Before you wire a new chip: 5 datasheet checks
bullets: Absolute maximum ratings: supply and pin voltage. Do not go above them, even for a moment.
Logic levels: is the chip's VIH below your MCU's VOH? If not, add a level shifter.
Reset state: which pins float or output at power-up? Add pull-ups or pull-downs for them.
Current: how much can a pin sink or source? Add resistors, or a driver for big loads.
Supply: decoupling cap values and power-up order. Put the caps next to the pins.
